question: What type of crystals build up in the joints of a person with gout?
explanation: Gout happens when monosodium urate crystals build up in and around the joints because of high levels of uric acid in the blood. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h1)

question: Which joint is most commonly affected during a first-time gout attack?

options.A: The middle joint of the hand
options.B: The base joint of the big toe

explanation: The joint at the base of the big toe is the classic spot where acute gout attacks usually start. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h1)

question: Uric acid is a waste product made from the breakdown of which chemical compounds?
explanation: Uric acid is formed when the body breaks down purines, which are found in certain foods and body cells. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h2)

question: Why do some people with high blood uric acid levels never actually get gout?

options.A: The liver destroys crystals before they reach joints
options.B: Drinking a lot of water stops uric acid from circulating
options.C: Uric acid must reach a high level to form crystals and cause inflammation
options.D: Kidneys block purines from entering joints

explanation: Having high uric acid is a risk factor, but crystals and pain only happen when the levels cross a certain saturation point. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h2)

question: What is the symptom-free time between acute gout attacks called?
explanation: The quiet periods between active gout flare-ups where the patient feels no pain are known as intercritical gout. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h3)

question: Which sign helps tell chronic tophaceous gout apart from earlier stages of the disease?

options.A: Completely normal blood uric acid levels
options.B: Pain that only affects the spine
options.C: Hard urate crystal deposits visible or felt under the skin
options.D: No inflammation at all during flares

explanation: Tophes are hard lumps of sodium urate crystals that form under the skin in advanced stages and can shape the joints. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h3)

question: Which type of medication is well-known for raising uric acid levels and triggering gout?
explanation: Diuretics make the kidneys get rid of less uric acid, which causes it to build up in the blood and can spark a gout attack. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h4)

question: Why do women before menopause generally have a lower risk of getting gout than men of the same age?

options.B: Estrogen helps the kidneys get rid of uric acid

explanation: Estrogen helps flush uric acid out of the body, giving women natural protection until they reach menopause. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h4)

question: What is the medical term for extreme skin sensitivity where even a light bedsheet causes severe joint pain during a gout flare?
explanation: Allodynia means feeling pain from something that normally does not hurt, which is common in inflamed gout joints. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h5)

question: A patient wakes up with a swollen, red, and very painful big toe. Which finding points to an acute gout flare instead of a simple injury?

options.A: Total numbness in the whole foot
options.B: Deep bruising spreading down the foot
options.C: Joint stiffness worsening slowly over months
options.D: Sudden, severe local swelling, redness, and heat

explanation: Gout attacks flare up very quickly within hours, bringing intense warmth, swelling, and redness to the joint. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h5)

question: What is considered the best test to confirm a diagnosis of gout?

options.D: Joint fluid analysis using a needle aspiration

explanation: Looking at joint fluid under a special microscope to find urate crystals gives a definite diagnosis for gout. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h6)

question: What common trap should a nurse watch out for regarding blood uric acid levels during an acute gout flare?

options.A: Levels always shoot up to maximum during pain
options.C: High uric acid always means a joint infection
options.D: Uric acid levels can look normal during an active flare

explanation: Uric acid levels in the blood can actually drop during a painful attack, so a normal lab result does not rule out gout. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h6)

question: Which medication is commonly given long-term to lower uric acid and prevent future gout attacks?
explanation: Allopurinol blocks the enzyme that makes uric acid, helping to keep blood levels low over the long term. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h7)

question: Why is it usually not advised to start long-term uric acid-lowering drugs right in the middle of a painful gout flare?

options.A: Pain relievers cancel out lowering drugs
options.B: Sudden changes in uric acid can move crystals and make the flare worse
options.C: Blood pressure drops dangerously if given together
options.D: Kidneys cannot filter any drugs during a flare

explanation: Starting these drugs during an attack can cause crystals to shift and break loose, making the pain last even longer. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h7)

question: What simple piece of equipment keeps heavy blankets off a painful, sensitive toe with gout?
explanation: A bed cradle holds the weight of the sheets up so they do not press on the tender, inflamed joint. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h8)

question: What advice should a nurse give a patient about drinking fluids to manage gout?

options.A: Drink plenty of water daily to help the kidneys flush out uric acid
options.B: Only drink water at night to stop daytime swelling
options.C: Restrict all fluids to protect the joints
options.D: Drink alcohol-free beer to replace electrolytes

explanation: Drinking lots of water dilutes the urine and helps the kidneys wash out uric acid before it can form crystals. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h8)

question: Which internal organ is prone to stones and damage when uric acid crystals build up over time?
explanation: High amounts of uric acid can lead to kidney stones and long-term kidney damage as crystals collect in the renal tract. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h9)

question: What is the main long-term goal of medical and lifestyle care for chronic gout?

options.A: Wrapping the joint in tight bandages forever
options.B: Keeping blood uric acid below the level that causes crystals to form
options.D: Cutting out all protein from the diet

explanation: Keeping uric acid levels low stops new crystals from forming and lets old ones safely dissolve over time. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h9)
